title: Prototype routing to isolated adapters on digits
setting: sklearn digits (64 px) are standardized and projected to a frozen 32-d PCA embedding (fit on train). Classes are split into T disjoint tasks. Each task gets its own logistic-regression adapter, and test chunks are routed to adapters via cosine similarity to per-task mean-embedding prototypes. The metric is class-incremental accuracy (10-way global label) on held-out test samples, averaged over tasks after the whole sequence; the replay baseline is a shared MLP trained sequentially with 20 stored samples per past task.

paper.title: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing
paper.claim: Training-free nearest-prototype routing of batches to isolated per-task adapters beats replay-based sequential training and approaches oracle task routing, with the advantage depending on prototype separability and routing batch size.

metric.name: final_average_accuracy
metric.description: Mean over tasks of held-out test accuracy (global 10-class label) after the full task sequence.

factors.name: method
factors.description: shared_replay: single MLP trained sequentially with a 20-per-past-task replay buffer; prototype_routing: CaLLM-style cosine nearest-prototype chunk routing to per-task adapters; oracle_routing: true task ID routing (upper bound for the adapters).

factors.name: task_count
factors.description: Number of tasks the 10 classes are split into (10 means one class per task, so accuracy equals routing accuracy).

factors.name: task_grouping
factors.description: clustered: tasks are contiguous groups of classes along the main axis of class-mean variation (distinct prototypes); interleaved: classes are dealt round-robin so task prototypes are close together and overlap.

factors.name: chunk_size
factors.description: Number of single-task test samples per routed chunk; small chunks give noisier batch-mean embeddings.
